The Log-Likelihood of a Fit

Source: R/report.R
logLik.StatmodFit.Rd

The value that R's convention expects, with the degrees of freedom and the number of observations as attributes. loglik() is a different function: it evaluates the model at parameters and data chosen by the caller.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'StatmodFit'
logLik(object, type = c("conditional", "marginal"), ...)

Arguments

object

A StatmodFit().

type

"conditional" (the default) or "marginal".

...

Unused.

Value

A logLik object: a single number with attributes df, the degrees of freedom, and nobs, the sum of the prior weights (the number of rows where the weights are all 1). stats::AIC() and stats::BIC() read it, so AIC(fit) is the conditional AIC.

Which likelihood, and why it matters

The default is the conditional one: the log-density at the fitted coefficients, a penalized coefficient among them, paired with the effective degrees of freedom \(\mathrm{tr}[(H+S)^{-1}H]\). A criterion built on that pair is the conditional AIC, which measures how well the model describes the groups, curves and states actually observed.

A mixed-model package reports the marginal likelihood instead: the random effects are integrated out and the count is the number of estimated parameters, variance components among them. That likelihood concerns the population, and the AIC built on it is a different number, not comparable with the conditional one.

Each likelihood keeps its own count. A marginal likelihood against an effective count, or a conditional one against a parameter count, mixes the two conventions (Vaida and Blanchard, 2005).

When the marginal one is available

type = "marginal" returns the value of the outer criterion at the fit. Its degrees of freedom count the parameters that the marginal model estimates: the coefficients that no penalty covers, the dimension of the null space of each penalty without a kink (the straight line of a smooth), the hyperparameters that the outer search or a path estimated, and the free parameters of a structural term. A held hyperparameter is not counted, and a hyperparameter shared by several terms is counted once. The other coefficients of a penalized term are integrated out and are not counted.

The value exists only where the outer criterion is ml() or reml(). Where no outer criterion ran, or where it is aic() or bic(), there is no marginal likelihood, and requesting one signals an error.

References

Vaida, F. and Blanchard, S. (2005). Conditional Akaike information for mixed-effects models. Biometrika, 92(2), 351–370.
